name: Townsfolk
about: Ordinary town people: polite to a stranger, curious, quick to fright. Plain frontier speech.

say: Afternoon.
Don't believe I know your face.
Mind the horse apples,
the street ain't been swept since spring.
If you're looking for the stage,
it don't keep to any schedule I ever saw.
New in town?
Well. Keep your iron holstered and you'll do fine.
Can't stop, I'm late as it is.
They say the bank's holding the railroad payroll this month.
Wouldn't want to be the fella guarding it.
The Dry Creek boys and the Vulture Ridge bunch
are at each other's throats again.
Make enough trouble and it won't be the sheriff who comes.
It'll be the cavalry out of Fort Garnet.
The doc'll patch up anybody who can pay.
Don't ask him where he learned.
Lord, don't shoot!
I don't want no trouble, mister!
Somebody fetch the sheriff!
